items.title: Bill Bourgeois Interview, 1959-12-10
items.q: Santo and Lester Bouchon, Jeff Riddick, Tink Morton, Monk Hazel, 1940. No, that's 49. I remember. Yeah, I remember.

ctx.x: Very good drummer. Was he a New Orleanian originally?
No he's from Shreveport, around that section. Yeah he's from around, Jeff Riddick and he I believe was from the same hometown. I think Shreveport.
Let's see, did we get a guitar player with the Owls?

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: Bill Bourgeois was there for a while too, playing in a mission.

ctx.x: Well, it just varied, but mainly in the 60s, I'd say.

Oh yes. Whenever, or whoever it was that, or was it, was it Eisenhower who declared that all men are born equal or words to that effect and it made it integration and when the white, when the blacks and the whites could mix on the buses and all that, that was when the black union, musicians union and the white musicians union merged. And that's why it's called local 174 496 496 496 496 was the black local here in New Orleans. Now it's all under the same office and everything with Dave Winstein, the president. And…
Bill Bourgeois was there for a while too, playing in a mission. Yeah.
